    How concentrated the predicted events are, against the observed ones

    concentrationOf.Rd

    A boosted model with few, shallow trees and shrinkage pulls predictions toward the mean, so it can spread the expected events more evenly over the pixel-years than they happen. This measures it on out-of-fold (or out-of-year) predictions, so a model is not credited for what it has seen. Pixel-years are ranked by the prediction, highest first; tied predictions share their events equally. With early stopping a fold's held-out rows also chose its number of rounds, so the lift, the Gini index and the deviance on them are slightly optimistic (the predicted share is a little more concentrated, the deviance a little lower, than for new data).

    concentrationOf(
  observed,
  expected,
  basis = "out-of-fold",
  top = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25)
)

    Arguments

    observed

    The observed count of each pixel-year (in the core, for ignitions).

    expected

    The out-of-fold prediction of each pixel-year, as a count in the same units (outOfFoldPrediction()).

    basis

    "out-of-year" or "out-of-fold": what the predictions are (runXGBOOST()).

    top

    The shares of the pixel-years of the lift table (the top 1, 5, 10 and 25%).

    Value

    A list: basis, n (pixel-years), observed and expected (the totals), lift (a data.frame with top, observed, the share of the observed events in the top top of the pixel-years, and predicted, the share of the predicted events there: predicted below observed means the model spreads them too evenly), gini (the Gini index of the observed and of the predicted counts across pixel-years: 0 is even, 1 is all in one; the model's below the observed means too even), and deviance, the mean Poisson deviance per pixel-year, 2 * (y * log(y / mu) - (y - mu)).
